Rashi on Nedarim 4b:10:1.hebrew: אלא - הכי אמר שמואל: טעמא דאמר נמי ״שאני אוכל לך״, הוא דאיהו אסור בלבד — דמתני' בנודר בלבד קאמר דאסור, דקתני: ״אסור״:
Rashi on Nedarim 4b:10:1.english: Rather - Shmuel said as follows: The reason is that he also said, "that which I eat of yours," [and] it is he alone who is forbidden, for the Mishnah spoke only of the one who vows being forbidden, as it teaches: "[he is] forbidden."

Rashi on Nedarim 4b:1:1.hebrew: שאם גילח על אחת משלשתן - דנזיר חייב שלש קרבנות: עולה, חטאת, ושלמים, כדכתיב: "והקריב את קרבנו לה' כבש בן שנתו תמים וגו'" (במדבר ו׳:י״ד). ואם לא הביא אלא חטאת, מגלח עליו — והיינו חידוש, משא"כ בשאר קרבנות. ולהכי, אימא: אינו עובר ב"בל תאחר", קמ"ל:
Rashi on Nedarim 4b:1:1.english: That if he shaved upon one of the three - For a nazirite is obligated to bring three offerings: a burnt-offering, a sin-offering, and a peace-offering, as it is written: “And he shall present his offering to the Lord: one unblemished yearling he-lamb...” (Numbers 6:14). And if he brought only a sin-offering, he shaves upon it, and this is a novelty, which is not the case with other offerings. And for this reason, one might say that he does not violate “You shall not delay”; therefore, it teaches us that he does violate it.

Rashi on Nedarim 4b:2:1.hebrew: ואב"א מאי חידושיה דאין מתפיסו בנדר - כדאמרינן לעיל, דאי אמר: "הרי עלי חטאת נזיר" — לא מתפיס ליה:
Rashi on Nedarim 4b:2:1.english: And if you wish, say: What is its novelty? That one cannot accept it through a vow - As we said above, that if one said: “Behold, upon me is a nazirite sin-offering,” the vow does not take effect upon it.

Rashi on Nedarim 4b:2:2.hebrew: אתיא לכפרה - דהאי צריך כפרה משום חלב שאכל, וכיון דלכפרה קא אתי — קאי בבל תאחר. אבל נזיר לא עביד שום חטא דליבעי כפרה:
Rashi on Nedarim 4b:2:2.english: [It] comes for atonement - For this [person] requires atonement on account of the forbidden fat that he ate, and since it comes for atonement, he is subject to [the prohibition of] “You shall not delay.” But a nazirite did not commit any sin that would require atonement.

Rashi on Nedarim 4b:4:1.english: Let it come through “what do we find” - In vows, a father nullifies the vows of his daughter.

Rashi on Nedarim 4b:5:1.hebrew: אבל גבי נזירות דאית ליה קיצותא - דכיון דלא מיתסר אלא עד אותו זמן, ימתין עד לזמן ולא ליעבור ליה. קא משמע לן היקישא — דא היקישא ליכא למיפרך כמו במה מצינו:
Rashi on Nedarim 4b:5:1.english: But with regard to naziriteship, which has a [time] limit - For since [she] is forbidden only until that time, let [him] wait until the time [elapses] and not revoke it. [Therefore,] the juxtaposition teaches us [that he may nullify it], for a juxtaposition cannot be refuted as [can an analogy of] mah matzinu.

Rashi on Nedarim 4b:6:1.hebrew: אמר שמואל בכולן - בכל הני דקתני במתני' — "מודר אני ממך", "מופרשני ממך" וכו' — לא הוי נדר; ועד שיאמר "שאני אוכל לך", לא מיתסר באותו דבר:
Rashi on Nedarim 4b:6:1.english: Shmuel said: In all of them - In all these [cases] taught in the Mishnah — "I am avowed from you," "I am separated from you," etc. — it is not a vow; and until he says "that I eat of yours," he is not forbidden from that thing.

Rashi on Nedarim 4b:7:1.english: This is what it is teaching - That is to say, [the baraita] is incomplete [and missing words].

Rashi on Nedarim 4b:7:2.hebrew: במה דברים אמורים - דאסור כי אמר: "מודר אני", באומר נמי: "שאני אוכל לך":
Rashi on Nedarim 4b:7:2.english: In what case is this statement said - That he is prohibited when he says: “I am avowed from you,” is when he also says: “That which I eat of yours.”

Rashi on Nedarim 4b:8:1.hebrew: והתניא איפכא - דלא מצית אמרת בד"א:
Rashi on Nedarim 4b:8:1.english: But isn’t it taught in the opposite order - For you cannot say: “In what case is this statement said?”

Rashi on Nedarim 4b:8:2.hebrew: תני הכי - דהכי קתני: ״שאני אוכל לך״ ו״שאני טועם״, וכבר אמר מעיקרא ״מודרני ממך״ — אסור. אבל אמר ״שאני אוכל לך״ בלבד או ״מודרני ממך״ — אינו אסור, אא"כ אמר לתרוייהו, דהיינו נדר גמור:
Rashi on Nedarim 4b:8:2.english: Teach [it] as follows - For this is what it teaches: “[That] which I eat of yours” and “[that] which I taste,” and he had already said beforehand “I am avowed from you” — [he is] prohibited. But [if] he said “[That] which I eat of yours” alone, or “I am avowed from you,” he is not prohibited, unless he said both of them, which is a complete vow.

Rashi on Nedarim 4b:9:1.english: If so, this is also the first baraita - For it taught "I am vow-separated from you" in the first baraita.

Rashi on Nedarim 4b:9:2.hebrew: ועוד - אי הכי הוא כדתרצת, תרי זימני ״אסור״ למה לי למיתני:
Rashi on Nedarim 4b:9:2.english: And furthermore - If it is so, as you resolved, why did [the baraita] need to teach "prohibited" two times?

Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:10:1.hebrew: אלא הכי קאמר טעמא [דאמר] בהדיא מודרני ממך שאני טועם לך הוא דאסור וחבירו מותר - דהכי משמע "אסור", מדלא קתני "שניהם אסורים". אבל "מודרני ממך" לחודיה — שניהם אסורין, ד"מודרני ממך" משמע: ממוני וממונך עלי. וברייתא דקתני "מודרני ממך אסור" — "שניהם אסורים" קאמר; והא דלא תני "שניהם אסורים" — משום דתנא ברישא "שאני טועם לך", דאז אינו אסור אלא מודר:
Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:10:1.english: Rather, this is what [Shmuel] is saying: The reason [that he said] explicitly "I am avowed from you [that] which I taste of yours" is that he is forbidden and his fellow is permitted - For this is what "forbidden" implies, since it did not teach "both of them are forbidden." However, [if he said] "I am avowed from you" alone, both of them are forbidden, for "I am avowed from you" implies: My property and your property are [forbidden] to me [and to you]. And the baraita that teaches "[If one says:] I am avowed from you, he is forbidden" means: both of them are forbidden. And that which it did not teach "both of them are forbidden" is because it taught in the first clause "that which I taste of yours," in which case only the one avowed is forbidden.

Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:1:1.hebrew: וכי גילח על אחת משלשתן יצא - כי נזיר היה לענין שמביא ג' קרבנות: חטאת, ועולה, ושלמים; ויצא — לענין שיהא מותר ביין; ולא לעבור משום "בל תאחר"? קמ"ל:
Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:1:1.english: "And if he shaved upon one of the three of them, he has fulfilled" - For a nazirite was obligated with regard to bringing three offerings: a sin-offering, a burnt-offering, and peace-offerings; and "he has fulfilled" his obligation is with regard to being permitted to drink wine; and lest you say that he should not violate the prohibition on account of "You shall not delay," it teaches us that he does violate it.

Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:2:1.hebrew: מאי חידושו דאין מתפיסו בנדר - דמכי הוי נזיר, ממילא חייב להביא קרבן:
Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:2:1.english: What is its novelty? That one does not obligate it through a vow - For once he becomes a nazirite, he is automatically obligated to bring an offering.

Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:2:2.hebrew: חטאת חלב לכפרה קאתי - ושייך בל תאחר, אבל נזיר לא לכפרה קאתי, ולכך ליכא בל תאחר:
Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:2:2.english: A sin-offering of forbidden fat comes for atonement - And the prohibition of "You shall not delay" applies, but the offering of a nazirite does not come for atonement, and therefore there is no prohibition of "You shall not delay".

Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:3:1.hebrew: והרי חטאת יולדת - דמשמע ליה דאיתא בכלל שאר חטאות. תימה: תיקשי ליה, אמאי איצטריך היקשא לקרבן יחיד, דליתיה בכלל שאר חטאות:
Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:3:1.english: "And behold, the sin-offering of a woman who gave birth" - For it implies to the Gemara that it is included in the general category of other sin-offerings. This is astonishing: let it raise the difficulty, why was the juxtaposition needed for an individual offering, implying that it is not included in the general category of other sin-offerings?

Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:3:2.hebrew: ההיא קא שריא ליה למיכל בקדשים - אע"ג דנזיר נמי שרי ליה (נמי) לשתות ביין — אין זה מצוה; אבל לאכול בקדשים מצוה היא, דכתיב: ״ואכלו אותם אשר כופר בהם״, הלכך שייך ביה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:3:2.english: "That [offering] permits her to eat consecrated food" - Even though [the offerings of] a nazirite also permit him to drink wine, this is not a mitzvah; but eating consecrated food is a mitzvah, as it is written: “And they shall eat those [offerings] with which atonement was made” (Exodus 29:33). Therefore, [the prohibition against delaying] applies to it.

Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:4:1.hebrew: למה לי היקשא - אבל לעיל גבי "בל תאחר" לא פריך, דאין עונשין מן הדין. אבל לא מצי למימר גבי "בל יחל" דאתי במה מצינו, דלא שייך; נמי הכא, דטעמא דמפר נדר משום עינוי נפש — גם בנזירות נמי יש עינוי נפש:
Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:4:1.english: Why do I need the juxtaposition? - However, earlier regarding "You shall not delay," [the Gemara] did not ask [this], because one does not penalize based on a logical derivation [ein onshin min hadin]. But one could not say regarding "He shall not profane" that it should come through a mah matzinu [analogy], as [that] is not applicable [there either]; and also here, since the reason [a father or husband] nullifies a vow is because of affliction of the soul, in naziriteship too there is affliction of the soul.

Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:5:1.hebrew: נדרים לית ליה קיצותא - ובנדרים, כי נדר סתם — לעולם הוא. אבל נזירות, אימא לא, דסתם נזירות שלשים יום. קמ"ל דהך עינוי נפש, ומיפר:
Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:5:1.english: "Vows have no limit" - And with vows, when one vows without specification, it is forever. But [with regard to] naziriteship, I might say no [he cannot nullify it], as an unspecified naziriteship is thirty days. [Therefore,] it teaches us that this [too] is an affliction of the soul, and he may nullify [it].

Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:6:1.hebrew: אמר שמואל בכולן עד שיאמר כו' - פירוש: דמודרני ממך לאו כלום לחודיה, אבל שאני אוכל לחודיה — ודאי אסור. ומתני' פירושי קמפרש לה: מודרני ממך — באומר שאני אוכל לך:
Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:6:1.english: "Shmuel said: In all of them, until he says, etc." - Explanation: For [saying] "I am avowed from you" on its own is nothing, but "that which I eat [of yours]" on its own is certainly forbidden. And the Mishnah explains it: "I am avowed from you" [applies] when one says, "that which I eat of yours."

Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:7:1.hebrew: מיתיבי מודרני ממך אסור - מדקאמר "אסור" אכל חד, משמע דבלא "שאני אוכל" קאמר. ומשני: בד״א קתני, דסיפא מפרש לרישא שאין אסור אא״כ אמר "שאני אוכל לך". והא קתני סיפא: "שאני אוכל לך", והכא ליכא למימר בד״א, דהא "שאני אוכל" לחודיה אמר — דדוקא לעיל דקתני ברישא "מודרני ממך" שייך למימר בד״א; אע״ג דבריי' אחריתי היא, קרי ליה סיפא, וכן איתא בפרק גט פשוט (בבא בתרא דף קסה) דקאמר "זהב בדינרים", ופריך: "אי הכי היינו רישא", אע״ג דהיינו ברייתא אחריתי. ומשני: "וכבר אמר מודרני ממך". תימה, שהרי "שאני אוכל לך" לחודיה אמר! וצ״ל דה״פ: "וכבר אמר" — כלומר אפילו אומר "מודרני ממך", דסד״א הואיל ו"מודרני ממך" לחודיה לא אסר, אפי' אמר אחריו "שאני אוכל לך" לא אסר; "וכבר אמר" — אפי' כבר אמר:
Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:7:1.english: "The Gemara raises an objection: 'I am avowed from you... he is prohibited'" - Since it says "he is prohibited" regarding each one, it implies that it means even without [saying] "that I eat [of yours]." And [the Gemara] answers that it teaches: "In what case is this statement said..." — that the latter clause explains the first clause, that he is not prohibited unless he said "that I eat of yours." [The Gemara then objects:] But isn't it taught in the latter clause: "That I eat of yours..."? And here one cannot say "In what case is this statement said...", for he said "that I eat" by itself! For only above, where it taught in the first clause "I am avowed from you," is it applicable to say "In what case is this statement said..." (even though it is a different baraita, [the Gemara] calls it the "latter clause"; and similarly it is found in the chapter [entitled] Get Pashut (Bava Batra 165b), where it says "gold in dinars" and objects: "If so, this is the first clause!" even though it is a different baraita). And [the Gemara] answers: "And he had already said 'I am avowed from you.'" [On this,] it is astonishing, for he said "that I eat of yours" by itself! And it must be said that this is its explanation: "And he had already said" — that is to say, even if he says "I am avowed from you" [as well]. For you might have thought that since "I am avowed from you" by itself does not prohibit, even if he said "that I eat of yours" after it, it would not prohibit; [therefore it teaches] "and he had already said" — [meaning] even if he had already said [it].

Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:9:1.hebrew: אי הכי היינו רישא - כלומר: אם בא התנא לאשמועינן דכ"ע עד שיאמר "שאני טועם לך", א"כ אמאי לא אמר כי האי לישנא של אידך ברייתא, ולא להקדים "שאני אוכל לך"? דאז ניחא למימר בד"א, שמפרש דאי אמר "שאני אוכל לך" לחודיה — דאינו אסור. וכן משמע דקמשני גבי "וכבר אמר מודרני ממך", וכן משמע דמתחילה הוה פריך ורוצה להוכיח ד"שאני אוכל" לחודיה מהני:
Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:9:1.english: If so, this is the first [baraita] - That is to say, if the Tanna came to teach us that everyone [agrees that a vow does not take effect] until he says: "That which I taste of yours," if so, why did he not state [it in] this phrasing of the other baraita, rather than putting "that which I eat of yours" first? For then it would be straightforward to say: "In what case is this said?" — which explains that if he said "that which I eat of yours" alone, he is not prohibited. And so it is indicated by that which [the Gemara] answers regarding: "And he had already said: I am avowed from you," and so it is indicated by the fact that initially [the Gemara] was objecting and wanting to prove that "that which I eat" alone is effective.

Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:9:2.hebrew: אי הכי היינו רישא - תימה: מאי "אי אמרת בשלמא" איכא הכא? וי"ל, דהכי פרושא: אי אמרת בשלמא דכל חד וחד מהני לחודיה — לא קשיא מידי, דליכא למיפרך "היינו רישא", דה"א דתנא סיפא לגלויי רישא; דאי לא תנא סיפא, הייתי מפרש דרישא ר"ל כגון שאמר "שאני אוכל לך" עם "מודרני ממך", קמ"ל סיפא דכל חד וחד לחודיה מהני:
Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:9:2.english: "If so, this is the first [baraita]" - It is puzzling: What "Granted, if you say..." is there here? And one can say that this is the explanation: Granted, if you say that each [phrase] on its own is effective, there is no difficulty at all, as one cannot object, "This is the first [baraita]!" — for I would have said that [the tanna] taught the latter [baraita] to clarify the first [baraita], for had he not taught the latter [baraita], I would have explained that the first [baraita] meant, for example, where he said "that which I eat of yours" together with "I am avowed from you"; [therefore,] the latter [baraita] teaches us that each one on its own is effective.

Tosafot on Nedarim 4b:9:3.english: "And furthermore, why do I need 'prohibited,' 'prohibited'?" - It is regarding the baraita that [the questioner] is saying this to him.
